the role of cortisol reactivity to stress in mediating the effects of early adversity on later maladaptive outcomes.

early adversity, cortisol reactivity, and maladaptive outcomes are related to prenatal substance exposure.
cortisol reactivity to stress mediates the effect of early adversity on adaptive outcomes.
early adversity, as measured by prenatal substance exposure and childhood neglect, predicts maladaptive outcomes in African Americans, and this relation may be mediated by cortisol reactivity.

early adversity is associated with increased cortisol reactivity to stress, which in turn is associated with maladaptive outcomes in African American youth.
the relation between early adversity and later maladaptive outcomes may be partially mediated by cortisol reactivity.
cortisol reactivity to social challenge may be one mechanism by which early adversity leads to risk and adaptive outcomes.
